questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Algeria?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Algeria article.

questions.proof: It has its capital and largest city as Algiers, which is in the far north.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Algeria?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Algeria on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Algeria article.

questions.proof: It is situated along the Mediterranean Sea with its borders being Tunisia, Libya, Niger, Mali, Mauritania, Western Sahara and Morocco.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Algeria?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Algeria article.

questions.proof: The Arabic and Tamazight languages are the official languages, but French is also commonly used.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Algeria?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Algeria article.

questions.proof: Currency: The currency is Algerian Dinar.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1830, Algeria was overrun by _____ and monitored a period of more than 130 years.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “overrun”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Algeria article.

questions.proof: In 1830, Algeria was overrun by France and monitored a period of more than 130 years.
